researcher: claude, read of the llama.cpp server README

facts.claim: llama-server listens on 127.0.0.1 by default; its own default port is 9931 and gt's farm engines run it on 8080, so the template default is the farm's port and the owner passes --base-url for another.
facts.evidence: README: by default listens on 127.0.0.1:9931; --host default 127.0.0.1, --port default 9931.

facts.claim: GET /health is public (no API key check) and returns 200 {"status": "ok"} when the model is loaded, or 503 with an error body while it is loading.
facts.evidence: README, GET /health: 'This endpoint is public (no API key check)'; ready 200 {"status": "ok" }; loading 503 'Loading model'.

facts.claim: The server offers OpenAI-compatible chat completions at /v1/chat/completions.
facts.evidence: README features list: 'OpenAI API compatible chat completions, responses, and embeddings routes'. The page does not document the response shape or a `usage` object with prompt_tokens and completion_tokens (the feature request says it does).

facts.claim: There is no key unless the server was started with --api-key (default: none); GET /props is read-only unless the server is started with --props.
facts.evidence: README: --api-key 'default: none'; /props 'By default, it is read-only'.

facts.claim: The server binds 127.0.0.1 by default, so a connection to it names only the loopback host; a remote engine is reached through an SSH tunnel to that loopback address.

choices.because: no key by default; LOTR allows plain http only to this machine, so a remote engine uses an SSH tunnel
public, answers 200 only when the model is loaded
a completion costs compute and is the call the farm makes

open: The `usage` object in a chat-completions reply is not in the README; token counts from it are unverified until read from a live reply.
GET /v1/models is listed as read-only but its response was not documented on the page read.
